reconcile.connective: Gill reads Proverbs' wicked-as-ransom as temporal substitution in judgment, expressly distinguishing it from Christ's atoning ransom for his people.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells's Skeptics Annotated Bible presses the four ransom texts as genuinely incompatible answers to a single question, not complementary senses.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Who (or what) is the ransom for the righteous?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com, est. 1999; print ed. SAB Books, 2013)

excerpts.excerpt_text: Not to make satisfaction for them, as Christ is a ransom for his people; but as a ransom is in the room of another, so the wicked cometh in the stead of the righteous, and into the trouble he is delivered from …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Gill's exposition on Prov 21:18 explicitly denies that the wicked's substitutionary suffering is the same kind of 'ransom' as Christ's satisfaction for his people, directly addressing the OT-wisdom-vs-Synoptic/Pastoral 'ransom' tension the question raises.

pd_work.resource: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63)
pd_work.author: John Gill
pd_work.note: Gill treats Proverbs 21:18 directly and distinguishes its wicked-as-ransom from Christ's atoning ransom -- the same passage anchoring this row's reconcile pole; Haley's Alleged Discrepancies could not be confirmed to treat this specific ransom cluster.
